title: Which of the following is the BEST description of a valid informed consent for a medical or surgical procedure?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A note in the medical record which is signed by the treating doctor, the patient, and a witness, in which the patient gives the doctor permission to treat them.
omfs: A witnessed discussion between the treating doctor and the patient in which the proposed treatment is discussed. The discussion should include a description of the procedure, the risks and benefits of the procedure, the likelihood of success of the procedure, and any alternatives to the treatment and the risks and benefits of those alternatives
midterm: A witnessed discussion between the treating doctor and the patient in which it is made clear that treatment must be provided - doing nothing is not an option.
column5: A pre-operative review of the doctor's previous consultation by the doctor or his/her designee in which all issues related to the procedure are discussed.
column6: A witnessed and documented discussion in which all issues discussed are initiated by the patient's questions so that the requirement to answer all of the patient's questions is clearly met.

title: A patient presents to your office for extraction of a tooth. You obtain a written and oral medical history which reveals the following information: • 70-year-old male • Myocardial infarction 3 years ago • 3 stents placed at that time • Ejection fraction 50 % • Develops shortness of breath when climbing more than 1 flight of steps • Takes insulin for diabetes What ASA classification would best describe his condition?
omfs: ASA II
midterm: ASA III
column5: ASA IV
column6: ASA V

title: Which of the following statements about patients with thrombocytopenia is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A patient may have a platelet deficiency, but as long as their platelet count is 50,000 or more, tooth extraction can generally be performed without significant bleeding risk.
omfs: If a patient with a history of thrombocytopenia has a normal platelet count for greater than two months, it can be assumed that their platelet count will stay in the normal range and surgery can be safely performed.
midterm: If tests reveal a normal platelet count on a patient with a known platelet disorder, tooth extraction can be performed without risk of bleeding.
column5: Liver disease is never a cause of an abnormal platelet count.
column6: If a patient has a history of thrombocytopenia but has a normal platelet count at the time of surgery, they can be given NSAIDs or aspirin for pain control in the peri-operative period.

title: Which of the following statements regarding management of anticoagulation with regard to the performance of oral surgery procedures is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A treating dentist should always advise a patient on warfarin to not take their warfarin for three days prior to an extraction.
omfs: The decision as to whether or not to hold off on taking targeted anticoagulants prior to tooth extraction should be based on the patient's INR three days before the procedure.
midterm: The MAPPP app is extremely useful because it gives treating dentists the information they need to manage their patients' anticoagulation without ever having to consult their patients' physicians.
column5: Decisions regarding the management of anticoagulation prior to tooth extraction should be based on the risk of bleeding with the specific procedure being performed and the risk of clotting complications if the anticoagulation therapy is interrupted. A decision to interrupt a patient's anticoagulation should be made in conjunction with the physician managing the anticoagulation.
column6: In this day and age, it is never necessary to alter a patient's anticoagulation regimen prior to oral surgical procedures because local adjunctive procedures and materials and reversal agents can be utilized to safely control all post-operative bleeding.

title: All of the following statements regarding oral surgery on patients who have conditions that may exacerbate their potential to bleed are TRUE, EXCEPT:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Patients with the potential to have bleeding problems should be taken care of early in the day and early in the week for elective and non-emergent situations.
omfs: If a patient with increased risk for bleeding requires multiple teeth to be extracted, it may be prudent to first perform a “test” surgery by extracting one or two teeth and seeing how they respond.
midterm: Local anesthetic that contains epinephrine should always be used on these patients as it will overcome the patient's risk for increased bleeding.
column5: Adjunctive local measures should be utilized to reduce the risk of harmful bleeding.
column6: When circumstances permit, oral surgical procedures should be scheduled at times when bleeding risk is less likely, such as before or after chemotherapy regimens, rather than while chemotherapy is being performed.

title: Which of the following practices would NOT be useful for minimizing the risk of vaso-vagal reactions?
omfs: Anxiety control
midterm: Pain control
column5: Administration of supplemental O2.
column6: Maintaining the patient in an upright position throughout the procedure.

title: Which of the following regimens is applicable for a patient with Type 1 diabetes in the peri-operative period?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: If the patient was able to eat breakfast and their post-operative oral intake will be impaired, then the patient should take their usual dose of regular insulin and one-half of their NPH dose.
omfs: If the patient is NPO, then they should take their usual dose of regular insulin and not take their NPH dose.
midterm: If the patient was able to eat breakfast and their post-operative oral intake will be impaired, then the patient should take one half of their dose of regular insulin and their usual NPH dose.
column5: If the patient is NPO, then they should not take their regular insulin but they should take their regular NPH dose.
column6: Whether or not the patient is able to eat before surgery, they should follow their usual insulin regimen as prescribed by their doctor.

title: Which of the following statements regarding oral surgery in HIV+ patients is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: HIV+ patients are at significantly increased risk of infection following oral surgical procedures.
omfs: Approximately 50 % of HIV+ patients have a decreased platelet count that puts them at significant risk of bleeding during and following oral surgical procedures.
midterm: Antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated for oral surgical procedures an HIV+ patient with a CD4+ count less than 200.
column5: Antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated for oral surgical procedures for an HIV+ patient with a neutrophil count less than 4000.
column6: HIV antiviral medications do not exhibit significant interactions with other medications that may be used by these patients.

title: Which of the following statements related to osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is NOT TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Removal of potential sources of infection such as carious or periodontally involved teeth before the initiation of radiation treatment is helpful in the prevention of ORN.
omfs: When extractions are performed prior to irradiation, sharp areas of bone should be smoothed as bone remodeling will not occur normally in irradiated bone.
midterm: When extractions are performed prior to irradiation, primary closure of soft tissue should be achieved when possible so that radiation therapy can be initiated as soon as possible.
column5: When extractions are performed prior to irradiation, a three-week waiting period prior to irradiation will generally be adequate. If soft tissue closure has not occurred, irradiation should be withheld until this is achieved, unless the risk of waiting longer is significant.
column6: Endodontic treatment of non-restorable teeth in irradiated patients is not beneficial as these procedures are associated with the same risk as extractions in these patients.

title: Which of the following statements regarding patients with adrenal suppression is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Secondary adrenal suppression is caused by any disease of the adrenal cortex which results in an inability to release endogenous corticosteroids in response to stress.
omfs: Complex prolonged surgery may result in hypertension, syncope, nausea, and hypothermia.
midterm: Supplemental steroids should be given for all patients with adrenal suppression for any surgical procedure.
column5: When supplemental steroids are necessary for a patient who is currently on steroids, the following regimen should be followed: Administer twice the patient's daily dose on pre-op, op, and post-op day 1, then resume the normal dose.
column6: When supplemental steroids are necessary for a patient who has taken 20 mg of hydrocortisone or its equivalent for two or more weeks within the previous year, the following regimen should be followed: Administer steroids for six weeks as follows: 60 mg of hydrocortisone daily for 2 weeks before the procedure, 40 mg daily for 2 weeks following the procedure, and then 20 mg daily for the following 2 weeks.

title: Several scenarios and management strategies regarding patients presenting for oral surgery are paired below. Which of the following management strategies DOES NOT MAKE SENSE for the scenario it accompanies?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A 22-year-old male professional bicycle racer presents with a blood pressure of 118/72 and a pulse of 48. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. Lidocaine with epinephrine can be administered for local anesthesia.
omfs: A 16-year-old girl who weighs 101 pounds presents with a blood pressure of 97/68 and a pulse of 102. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. Mepivaciane can be administered for local anesthesia.
midterm: A 72-year-old male with a history of hypertension presents with a blood pressure of 162/94 and a pulse of 84. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. Either mepivacaine or up to two carpules of lidoocaine with epinephrine can be administered for local anesthesia.
column5: A 78-year-old female with a history of hypertension presents with a blood pressure of 212/112 and a pulse of 92. She is complaining of pain in one of her maxillary molars and feels the tooth is causing her to have a headache. Treatment should not be provided at this time. The dentist should arrange for immediate evaluation and treatment of the patient's blood pressure.
column6: An anxious 16-year-old boy presents with a blood pressure of 122/72 and a pulse of 138. Treatment can be provided as these vital signs do not indicate a problem for this patient. lidocaine with epinephrine can be administered for local anesthesia.

title: A patient with a history of angina presents for extraction of a tooth. All of the following management strategies can be used by a general dentist, EXCEPT:
omfs: Monitor the patient's vital signs before, during, and following the procedure.
midterm: Use techniques to minimize the patient's anxiety.
column5: Administer nitroglycerin if the patient experiences an episode of angina.
column6: Maximize pain control.
column7: Limit or avoid epinephrine use with local anesthetics.
column9: Refer the patient to an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon for tooth extraction.
column10: All of these strategies can be used.

title: When treating an asthmatic patient, which of the following is NOT a helpful strategy/management technique?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Determine the severity and risk related to their asthma by obtaining a history including information about the frequency and severity of their episodes; whether they have presented to an Emergency Department, been hospitalized, or intubated for their asthma; what triggers their asthma; and when their most recent episode was.
omfs: If an asthma attack does occur intraoperatively, immediately administer cromolyn sodium to treat the patient.
midterm: Use a bronchodilator pre-operatively prophylactically and intra-operatively if an episode occurs.
column5: Assess the patient for wheezing pre- and intra-operatively.
column6: If general anesthesia is being contemplated, consult the patient's physician regarding the risks associated with the general anesthesia.
column7: When choosing post-operative analgesics, be aware that some asthmatics have an increased risk for aspirin allergy.

title: When general dentists are making decisions on the appropriate treatment for medically compromised patients that they may be taking care of, which of the following is NOT a legitimate consideration?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: The general dentist's level of experience and expertise regarding the necessary procedure.
omfs: Relative or absolute medical contraindications to the proposed surgery or anesthesia that may necessitate a change in the planned procedures.
midterm: “Modification” of the patient's condition and/or management so that surgery may be safely performed.
column5: Referral to an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon may be the best option for treatment.
column6: Consultation with the patient's physician may be necessary prior to treatment.
column7: General dentists should never perform surgical procedures on medically compromised patients.

title: Which of the following layers is NOT included in the flap when a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap (FTMPF) is elevated?
omfs: Bone.
midterm: Submucosa.
column5: Periosteum.
column6: Mucosa, submucosa, periosteum, and bone are all included in the flap.

title: When developing a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap (FTMPF) with 2 releasing incisions, the flap should be broader at the free gingival margin than at the base.
omfs: False.

title: Which of the following flaps/incisions should generally NOT be used during extractions?
omfs: 3 corner flap.
midterm: Semilunar incision.
column5: Submarginal incision.
column6: Semilunar and submarginal incisions.

title: When making a vertical releasing incision during dentoalveolar surgery, the incision should be placed:
omfs: At the tip of the papilla.
midterm: At the line angle of the tooth.
column5: Directly over the area of pathology.
column6: Across the root just crossing the apex.
column7: Just over or anterior to the mental foramen when extracting a mandibular bicuspid.

title: It is June 2018. While extracting a tooth and doing everything the way you were taught, much to your surprise, the tooth fractures. Before calling your instructor over, you start thinking about what the best treatment would be at this time. You remember that the apical portion of a tooth can be left in place if:
omfs: It has a radiolucency at the apex of the root.
midterm: It is greater than 4 to 5 mm in length.
column5: It is close to a vital structure.
column6: The patient would have no way of ever finding out that it was there.

title: Which of the following terms does NOT refer to a portion of a suture needle?
omfs: Body.
midterm: Shank.
column5: Point.

title: Which of the following suture materials is non-resorbable?
omfs: Silk.
midterm: Chromic gut.
column5: Plain gut.
column6: None of the above.

title: When penetrating a soft tissue flap with a suture needle, the angle of penetration is…
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: important and ideally it should enter the tissue perpendicular to the flap.
omfs: important and ideally it should enter the tissue at an acute angle to the flap.
midterm: important and ideally it should enter the tissue at an obtuse angle to the flap.
column5: important, but it will vary based on the location and type of flap.
column6: not important. It should enter the tissue at whatever angle is most comfortable for the operator.

title: A flap should be designed so that all of the incisions can be closed over bone.
omfs: False.

title: A surgical handpiece should be used during surgical procedures to section teeth and cut bone instead of a regular dental handpiece that is used for operative dentistry, because:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A surgical handpiece expels air from the rear of the handpiece to prevent air emphysema from occurring.
omfs: A surgical handpiece is longer than a regular dental handpiece, providing better access for reaching the apical portion of teeth.
midterm: A surgical handpiece expels air around the bur so that it keeps the surgical field clear, providing better visibility.
column5: A surgical handpiece expels air around the bur so that it clears the surgical field of debris, minimizing the risk of infection.
column6: Either a surgical handpiece or a regular dental handpiece can be used during surgical procedures.

title: What happens to the alveolar bone and soft tissues after teeth are extracted?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: The bone contour changes but the soft tissue contour does not.
omfs: The soft tissue contour changes but the bone contour does not.
midterm: Both bone and soft tissue contour changes take place.
column5: Neither bone or soft tissue contour changes take place.
column6: Periosteum and bone changes occur, but mucosal changes do not.

title: When evaluating patients for pre-prosthetic surgery, it is always necessary to:
omfs: Palpate the hard and soft tissues.
midterm: Perform a radiographic exam.
column5: Obtain a CBCT.
column6: Three of the above.

title: Which of the following statements regarding an epulis fissuratum is TRUE:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: The etiology can be a poor fitting denture.
omfs: The etiology can be a retained root tip.
midterm: Excision of the lesion is curative.
column5: Excision of the lesion alone is not curative - radiation is also necessary.
column6: Excision of the lesion alone is not curative - chemotherapy is also necessary.
column7: Excision of the lesion alone is not curative - radiation and chemotherapy are both also necessary.

title: Which of the following techniques and information are routinely required by a well-trained dentist to diagnose the condition of a patient's tooth and determine what treatment options are indicated? • I. Radiographic imaging. • II. Chief complaint and related history. • III. Clinical examination. • IV. Clinical research. • V. Literature review.
omfs: I, II, and IV.

title: Which of the following instruments are used for retracting? • I. Weider • II. Minnesota • III. Seldin • IV. 301 • V. 46R
omfs: I, III, and IV
midterm: III, IV, and V.
column5: I, II, IV, and V.
column6: I, II, III, and IV.

title: What is a No 9 Molt periosteal elevator used for?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: To make an incision through periosteum.
omfs: To reflect mucosa and periosteum.
midterm: To elevate a tooth from the periodontal ligament.
column5: To suture periosteum to mucosa.
column6: To administer local anesthesia.

title: Which is the most common scalpel blade used to make an incision in oral surgery?

Your “first-day-on-the-job” dental assistant is setting up an instrument tray for you to use to extract tooth #8. He asks you in what order you like your instruments to be placed on the tray. Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Scalpel, periosteal elevator, straight elevator, upper ash forceps, rongeur.

column6: Scalpel, periosteal elevator, straight elevator, rongeur, upper ash forceps.

title: It is May 2020. You are on your final TCDM Oral Surgery Rotation. Your schedule includes five patients requiring extractions as described below. Which patient/tooth scenario would you anticipate will be the MOST DIFFICULT surgical procedure that you are being asked to perform that day?

omfs: Extraction of erupted maxillary second premolar on a 12-year-old female.

column5: Extraction of mandibular first molar on a 54-year-old female with MIO (maximum interincisal opening) of 10mm.
column6: Extraction of mobile mandibular central incisor on an 85-year-old male on warfarin with an INR of 1.9.

title: Which of the following is most helpful in removing and contouring bone around the socket of an extracted tooth?
omfs: Curette.
midterm: Rongeur.
column5: Irrigation.
column6: No 65.

title: A mandibular first molar with a severely carious crown is being extracted. Which of the following techniques should NOT be used in the removal of this tooth?
omfs: Removal of the thin lingual cortical plate of bone.
midterm: Elevation of the individual roots with east-west elevators.
column5: Sectioning the tooth into separate mesial and distal roots.
column6: Reflecting a modest buccal flap and removing the most minimal amount of buccal bone necessary to accomplish the extraction.

omfs: Tooth #27.

title: (Bonus Question) You are on your Oral Surgery Rotation at Touro Dental Health. An emergency patient presents complaining of several days of pain of increasing severity from a carious non-restorable tooth. You review the patient's medical history, obtain informed consent, and administer mepivacaine so that you may perform an extraction. As you are about to begin the extraction, the patient's wife comes in and asks the patient if he remembered to tell you that he started warfarin several weeks ago for atrial fibrillation. You want to help the patient out so you:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Extract the tooth, supplementing the mepivacaine with lidocaine with epinephrine to minimize bleeding, tell the patient not to take his warfarin for three days, and give him detailed post-operative instructions regarding bleeding control. Advise the patient to take acetaminophen for his post-operative pain.
omfs: Tell the patient to take ibuprofen for his pain and not take his warfarin for three days and re-schedule the extraction in three days.
midterm: Tell the patient to take acetaminophen for his pain and not take his warfarin for three days and re-schedule the extraction in three days.
column5: Call the patient's physician to see if he knows the patient's platelet count. Based on this information decide with the physician how to manage the patient's warfarin and when to perform the extraction. Advise the patient to take acetaminophen for his pain.
column6: Check the patient's INR and find out that it is 2.0. Tell the patient it is his lucky day. Proceed with the extraction and take local measures to maximize hemostasis. Advise the patient to take acetaminophen for his post-operative pain.
